title: Metroid Prime Pinball
subtitle: Samus becomes the ball

body: Metroid Prime Pinball is Fuse Games' Nintendo DS reinterpretation of Samus Aran's first Prime adventure as a pinball game. Samus remains in Morph Ball form while familiar locations become tables filled with ramps, bumpers and enemies. The two displays form a tall playing field, and the touchscreen lets the player nudge the table to influence her path. The connection is unusually direct: an ability already central to Metroid becomes the physical object around which a different genre can be built.

Pirate Frigate and Tallon Overworld introduce a journey that opens further tables, including Phendrana Drifts and Phazon Mines. Completing objectives and minigames or defeating bosses earns artifacts. Samus can also use weapons and perform actions beyond an ordinary ball's movement, including wall jumps. That variety gives the tables tasks to pursue alongside the score. A promising shot may begin a fight, open another opportunity or advance the artifact collection, so keeping the ball alive supports a small adventure across recognisable locations.

Collecting twelve artifacts leads to the Artifact Temple, where a six-ball challenge asks the player to strike twelve targets while Meta Ridley attacks. Pinball's rising disorder becomes a suitable climax for the adapted journey. The game was also bundled with the DS Rumble Pak, adding a physical response to collisions and action. Its use of the handheld is economical: the screens provide height, the stylus supplies a nudge and the vibration gives the table an extra sense of impact without abandoning the familiar flippers.
